notes: ACCESS: Claude-in-Chrome only, own tab, no HTTP-layer fetching. robots.txt was checked in the prior pass (generic 'User-agent: *' with only /search /checkout /cart /customer /login /api /admin disallowed; no Claude-specific rule) - not re-fetched. TREE: three sources unioned. (1) SSR mega-menu JSON from the Next.js flight payload (self.__next_f, key 'headerMainMenu') which carries a 'count' per level-2 node; (2) /sitemap.xml, which yields all 97 /en/category/ URLs including every level-3 node; (3) the site's own per-category 'subCategory' list from api.chattelsandmore.com/api/category-product-filters/{id}/{slug}. All three agree; the sitemap and the filters endpoint gave the level-3 nodes the mega-menu only exposes for Sofas. COUNTS: the storefront is a client-side-rendered SPA and prints NO product-count header anywhere (checked the rendered Sofas and Sofa Beds pages) so Rule-1 header text does not exist here. Counts come from the site's own backend, GET api.chattelsandmore.com/api/category-products/{id}/{slug}?locale=en&per_page=1&page=1 -> data.meta.total, called same-origin from the loaded page. Corroboration: every level-2 total returned by that API matches the SSR mega-menu 'count' exactly (13/13 furniture nodes, two independent code paths); at level 3 the method was validated against the rendered page twice - Sofa Beds meta.total=3 equals the 3 product tiles rendered, and Lamp Tables meta.total=0 equals the site's rendered empty-state text. BAD-SLUG TRAP: tested - the API keys on the numeric id, not the slug. id 3 with a bogus slug still returns Sofas' 80, and a bogus id 99999 returns total 0 rather than falling back to a parent, so no plausible-wrong-number path exists. Every emitted frontend URL is present in the sitemap and two were opened directly, both with the correct h1 and self-referencing canonical. DEPTH DECISIONS: level 3 on this site is a partial facet layer - children never exceed the parent but always under-cover it. Where the children are genuine product types and cover the parent well I went deep and made the parent a grouping row: Sofas 79/80, Coffee & Side Tables 103/107, Stools & Ottomans 41/42, Storage & Home Office 61/69, Armchairs 56/74, Consoles & Sideboards 50/60. Where the children are material/form cuts that leave most of the parent unassigned I kept the parent as the leaf and flagged it: Dining Tables (children 31/73), Dining Chairs (52/78), Beds (6/12), Wardrobes (only child empty). Nightstands, Dressers and TV Stands & Media Consoles have no children at all. Never emitted a parent-as-leaf together with its children. Emitted total 583 of the site's 625 furniture products; the 42-product gap is the unassigned remainder inside the six go-deep parents. BRAND FACET EXCLUDED: the payload also carries 'headerMainMenuKare' - a parallel KARE-brand cut of the same catalogue (Sofas 7, Armchairs 44, Dining Tables 52 ...), served at /en/kare/category/...; every KARE count is a strict subset of the main count, so it is a brand filter over the same product ids, not extra inventory. Not emitted. EXCLUDED AS OUT OF SCOPE (all inspected in the sitemap/mega-menu): Dinnerware and its 7 children, Table Linen, Bed Linen, Pillows, Mattress, Galleries & Wall Art, Carpets & Rugs, Cushions, Decorative Accessories and its 5 children, Mirrors, Faux Trees & Plants, Plaids, Fragrances, Lighting (Floor / Ceiling / Table Lamps), Bathroom (Towels, Bath Robes - no bathroom furniture on this site). There is no outdoor/garden, kids/nursery or office-furniture department beyond Storage & Home Office.
